name: INTREPID
fullName: Fever Prevention in Patients With Acute Vascular Brain Injury
population: n=677, median 62; 51% female, NIHSS critically ill: 254 ischemic stroke, 223 ICH, 200 SAH, up to 14 days or ICU discharge
finding: Fever burden reduced: daily mean 0.37 vs 0.73 °C-hour
teachingPoint: Device-based fever prevention reduced fever burden but did not improve 3-month function; halted for futility.

name: SETPOINT2
fullName: Early vs Standard Approach to Tracheostomy in Severe Stroke Receiving Mechanical Ventilation
population: n=382, median 59; 49.8% women, NIHSS severe acute ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke requiring invasive ventilation, Randomized within 4 days of intubation; functional outcome at 6 months
finding: No significant benefit: mRS 0-4 in 43.5% vs 47.1% (difference −3.6%, 95% CI −14.3% to 7.2%); wide CI cannot exclude clinically relevant benefit or harm
teachingPoint: The early strategy did not demonstrate improved six-month outcome. It does not establish an individual recovery ceiling or prove that every patient can safely avoid tracheostomy.
